Difference in differences with two-way fixed effects

Source: R/policy_evaluation.R
plndid.Rd

The effect of a policy on a unit-by-period panel (municipalities by month, blocks by quarter, courts by year), from a regression of the outcome on the treatment indicator with unit and period fixed effects, and standard errors clustered by unit or by any coarser grouping.

Usage

plndid(
  data,
  unit,
  time,
  y,
  trtd,
  covs = NULL,
  cl = NULL,
  fe = c("unit", "time"),
  w = NULL,
  comb = NULL,
  conflvl = 0.95
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per unit and period.

unit, time, y

Column names: the unit, the period (numeric, for example a year or a month index) and the outcome.

trtd

Column name of the treatment indicator (0 or 1).

covs

Optional column names of time-varying controls.

cl

Column name of the clusters (default the unit), or two column names for two-way clustering (Cameron, Gelbach and Miller 2011): \(V_a + V_b - V_{ab}\), each term with the small-sample factor of the dimension with fewer clusters, and t on its \(G - 1\) degrees of freedom. A composite cluster (district by month, say) is one column made with interaction(). Fewer than ten clusters give a warning (CR1 errors are unreliable with so few; wcb is made for that case), and so does a cluster that changes within a unit.

fe

c("unit", "time") (default) or "time".

w

Optional column name of non-negative weights, such as population or matching weights, for weighted least squares with weighted within-means. Rows of weight 0 take no part in the fit.

comb

Optional linear combination of the terms, named by them, reported with its delta-method standard error as the attribute combined. For a phase-in model with an exposure term \(E_{it} = \min(t - G_i, K)\), comb = c(treated = 1, exposure = 12) is the effect after twelve periods, with its error, and as a percentage of the comparison units' pre-period mean (that mean taken as fixed).

conflvl

Confidence level of the intervals reported (default 0.95).

Value

A data frame of class rmbl_did, one row per term (the treatment first, then the covariates): term, estimate, se, lower, upper, t, p_value. Attributes: n, clusters, ctlmean (the pre-period mean of the comparison units), releff (the estimate over it), vcov, and with comb also combined.

Details

The model is $$Y_{it} = \beta T_{it} + X_{it}'\gamma + \delta_i + \mu_t + \varepsilon_{it},$$ fitted by ordinary least squares after the within transformation (alternating projections, so an unbalanced panel is fine). The variance is the one-way cluster-robust CR1 estimator, $$\hat V = \frac{G}{G - 1}\frac{N - 1}{N - K} (\tilde X'\tilde X)^{-1} \Big(\sum_g \tilde X_g'\hat u_g \hat u_g'\tilde X_g\Big) (\tilde X'\tilde X)^{-1},$$ with \(K\) counting the regressors and the fixed effects not nested in the clusters, and tests and intervals use Student's t on \(G - 1\) degrees of freedom. These are the conventions of Stata's reghdfe and R's fixest.

The relative effect is \(\hat\beta\) over the mean outcome of the units never treated (or not yet treated) in the periods before the first treatment, the way an effect on a rate is usually reported ("a 12% fall").

With fe = "time" the unit effects are left out, and the model is the cross-section with period effects of a comparison between kinds of units (for example blocks in dynastic and in other wards).

When treatment starts at different times, this estimator weights earlier-treated units as controls for later ones, and can be biased if the effect changes over time: see bacondcmp for the weights and stgatt for estimators that avoid them.

References

Bertrand M, Duflo E, Mullainathan S (2004). How much should we trust differences-in-differences estimates? Quarterly Journal of Economics 119(1):249-275. doi:10.1162/003355304772839588

Cameron AC, Gelbach JB, Miller DL (2011). Robust inference with multiway clustering. Journal of Business and Economic Statistics 29(2):238-249. doi:10.1198/jbes.2010.07136

Cameron AC, Miller DL (2015). A practitioner's guide to cluster-robust inference. Journal of Human Resources 50(2):317-372. doi:10.3368/jhr.50.2.317

Applied to a staggered criminal-procedure reform, municipality by month: Acosta C, Mejia D, Zorro Medina A (2023). On the tension between due process protection and public safety: the case of an extensive procedural reform in Colombia. doi:10.2139/ssrn.4585682

See also

evstudy, stgatt, perminf, plnpois.

Examples

p <- polex()
plndid(p, "district", "month", "crmrate", "reformed")
#> ╭── Difference in differences ────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Method           fixed-effects least squares, cluster-robust (CR1) errors │
#> │   Observations     720                                                      │
#> │   Clusters         20                                                       │
#> │   Confidence       95%                                                      │
#> │   Comparison mean  26.52                                                    │
#> │   Relative effect  -12.2% of the comparison mean                            │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   Estimates                                                                 │
#> │   term     estimate      se  95% CI                 t  p_value              │
#> │   -------  --------  ------  ----------------  ------  -------              │
#> │   treated    -3.232  0.1164  [-3.475, -2.988]  -27.76  < 0.001              │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   The policy's effect on the outcome is -3.232 (95% interval [-3.475,       │
#> │   -2.988]): the interval excludes 0, so the data distinguish it from no     │
#> │   effect.                                                                   │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   The comparison mean is the pre-period mean outcome of the units not       │
#> │   (yet) treated.                                                            │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
# clustered by region instead of district: only four regions, so the
# package warns, and wcb() is the tool for so few clusters
plndid(p, "district", "month", "crmrate", "reformed", cl = "region")
#> Warning: plndid: `cl` (region) gives only 4 clusters: cluster-robust (CR1) standard errors are unreliable with so few; wcb() is made for this case
#> ╭── Difference in differences ────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Method           fixed-effects least squares, cluster-robust (CR1) errors │
#> │   Observations     720                                                      │
#> │   Clusters         4                                                        │
#> │   Confidence       95%                                                      │
#> │   Comparison mean  26.52                                                    │
#> │   Relative effect  -12.2% of the comparison mean                            │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   Estimates                                                                 │
#> │   term     estimate      se  95% CI                 t  p_value              │
#> │   -------  --------  ------  ----------------  ------  -------              │
#> │   treated    -3.232  0.1656  [-3.759, -2.705]  -19.52  < 0.001              │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   The policy's effect on the outcome is -3.232 (95% interval [-3.759,       │
#> │   -2.705]): the interval excludes 0, so the data distinguish it from no     │
#> │   effect.                                                                   │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   The comparison mean is the pre-period mean outcome of the units not       │
#> │   (yet) treated.                                                            │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

# your own panel: eight towns over ten years, four adopting a by-law (two
# in 2019, two in 2021), with each town's population, county and income
own <- data.frame(
  town = rep(c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G", "H"), each = 10),
  year = rep(2015:2024, times = 8)
)
i <- match(own$town, unique(own$town))
own$first <- c(2019, 2019, 2021, 2021, NA, NA, NA, NA)[i]
own$bylaw <- as.integer(!is.na(own$first) & own$year >= own$first)
own$pop <- c(12, 30, 8, 22, 15, 40, 9, 18)[i] * 1000
own$county <- rep(c("North", "South"), 4)[i]
own$income <- 50 + own$year - 2015 + cos(seq_len(80))
own$rate <- 30 + i + 0.5 * (own$year - 2015) - 4 * own$bylaw +
  0.2 * own$income + sin(seq_len(80))
# the effect of the by-law, with income as a control, clustered by town
# (the default), weighted by population
plndid(own, "town", "year", "rate", "bylaw", covs = "income", w = "pop")
#> ╭── Difference in differences ────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Method           fixed-effects least squares, cluster-robust (CR1) errors │
#> │   Observations     80                                                       │
#> │   Clusters         8                                                        │
#> │   Confidence       95%                                                      │
#> │   Comparison mean  47.43                                                    │
#> │   Relative effect  -8.3% of the comparison mean                             │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   Estimates                                                                 │
#> │   term     estimate      se  95% CI                 t  p_value              │
#> │   -------  --------  ------  ----------------  ------  -------              │
#> │   treated    -3.914  0.1702  [-4.316, -3.511]  -22.99  < 0.001              │
#> │   income      0.227  0.0367  [0.140, 0.313]      6.17  < 0.001              │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   The policy's effect on the outcome is -3.914 (95% interval [-4.316,       │
#> │   -3.511]): the interval excludes 0, so the data distinguish it from no     │
#> │   effect.                                                                   │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   The comparison mean is the pre-period mean outcome of the units not       │
#> │   (yet) treated.                                                            │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
